alewife ale·wife | ˈālˌwīf | noun (plural alewives | ˈālˌwīvz |) a northwestern Atlantic fish of the herring family that swims up rivers to spawn and is found also in the Great Lakes. Alosa pseudoharengus, family Clupeidae • another term for menhaden ORIGIN mid 17th century: possibly from earlier alewife ‘woman who keeps an ale house’, with reference to the fish's large belly.
